author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hong Kong’s renewed deal activity is pulling financial professionals back to the city as initial public offerings and other fundraising recover. Total capital raised in the first eight months of 2026 reached $83.5 billion, Reuters reported, an increase of 76% from the same period a year earlier.

The expansion is spreading beyond trading desks. More than 400 companies established or enlarged Hong Kong operations during the first half, up 9% from a year earlier. Those commitments are expected to bring HK$53 billion, or about $6.8 billion, in direct investment and create roughly 8,600 jobs. The city’s economy grew 5.9% in the first quarter, adding momentum to the hiring rebound.

Office data provide another sign of firmer demand. Savills said prime Central rents rose 4.8% in the second quarter as vacancy fell to 9.4% from 10.2%; Knight Frank measured a decline from 14.5% at the start of the year to 9.7% in July. High living costs and closer integration with mainland China remain considerations, but the financing surge is improving Hong Kong’s appeal relative to Singapore, London and Dubai.
dek: A surge in fundraising and company expansion is supporting hiring and tightening premium office space after a prolonged slowdown.
headline: Hong Kong IPO rebound draws finance talent back
